title: Exact Stored Visit Code
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state binary Turing machine, let $C,e,c,A,d$ be natural numbers, let $x$ be a bit string, and let $j,t$ be natural numbers. If $t$ is at most the producer horizon for these parameters and $|x|$, then for every work tape $	au$ of $M$, the stored visit code at time $t$ in the packed records with cursor $j$ equals the optional-time code for the greatest time $s<t$ at which that tape's head, on the all-zero input of length $|x|+C(|x|+1)^e$, occupies its position at time $t$; it is the absent-visit code if no such time exists.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite-state binary Turing machine
$t$ is at most the producer horizon at input length $|x|$
$	au$ is a work tape of $M$
replaced: For every source machine, parameters, instance $x$, cursor $j$, time $t$ at most the producer horizon, and tape $\tau$, the stored visit code equals the optional-time code of the public greatest strictly earlier visit; the reference machine is never rerun and the protected table is never replaced.
